title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 3: mortal king cannot inspire victory-powers — if he could, not from foresight
pass_a_gloss: But the reason is this: Because it is not in the power of a mortal king to inspire and infuse that will, and those powers, from which infallibly this singular person rather than others obtains the victory. If he could do this, nothing would hinder but that to whichever friend of his he might from a primary and gratuitous will intend and decree to give that prize, yet so that he should arrive at it according to the law laid down, namely by conquering, and that from powers inspired into him by virtue of that primary intention. If the matter so stood in an earthly Prince, he would not be said to have elected his friend to obtaining the prize from foresight of merits, but from an antecedent purpose and intention of giving the prize, to have given the merits, and in this his donation to have foreseen. But that God so acts with all who are to be glorified is confessed.
pass_b_english: The reason: a mortal king cannot inspire and pour in the will and powers by which this one person rather than others infallibly wins. If he could, nothing would stop him intending and decreeing from a primary, gratuitous will to give that prize to any friend — yet so the friend reaches it by the stated law, namely by winning, and from powers inspired by that primary intention. Were an earthly prince so able, we would not say he elected his friend to the prize from foresight of merits, but that from an antecedent purpose to give the prize he gave the merits and in that gift foresaw them. And that God so deals with all who are to be glorified is confessed.
source_text: Ratio autem haec est; Quia non est penes Regem mortalem inspirare & infundere illam voluntatem, & illas vires ex quibus infallibiliter haec singularis persona prae aliis obtineat victoriam. Si hoc posset, nihil impediret, quin cuicunque amico suo ex primaria & gratuita voluntate intenderet & decerneret dare illud premium, ita tamen ut perveniret ad illud secundum legem positam, nimirum vincendo, idque ex viribus illi inspiratis virtute primariae illius intentionis. Si ita res se haberet in terreno Principe, non ex praevisione meritorum elegisse diceretur amicum suum ad premium obtinendum, sed ex antecedente proposito & intentione dandi premium, dedisse merita, & in hac sua donatione praevidisse. At sic agere Deum cum omnibus glorificandis in confesso est.
